title: Agent task contract
description: The record a runner enforces. A plan that is only prose can be followed loosely and nobody can tell afterwards; this shape is what atlas.yaml/agent_policy decides against, and the same record carries the outcome so the plan and the result are one artifact rather than two that may disagree.

schema.description: The contract format. A runner that does not recognise it refuses rather than guessing which fields it understands.

task_id.description: Stable across the whole task, and the name of its audit stream.

atlas_version.description: The contract version the plan was resolved at. A plan resolved against an older atlas is stale, and a runner says so rather than applying today's gates to yesterday's plan.

objective.description: One sentence. What would make this task DONE.

target.description: The artifact the route was resolved from, when the task has one.

route.description: A key of atlas.yaml/artifact_routes' targets, as `atlas.py route` resolved it.

change_class.description: A key of atlas.yaml/verification_policy/profiles. The floor; modifiers only add to it.

risk_modifiers.description: Keys of atlas.yaml/risk_modifiers whose applies_to is this change class.

required_gates.description: The gates the class and its modifiers resolved to. Planned here; each one's exit code is recorded in outcome.gates, so a gate that was never run cannot read as one that passed.

allowed_paths.description: Repository-relative prefixes. Everything else is refused, including reads: a task that reads what it was not scoped to has already expanded.

forbidden_paths.description: Refused even when an allowed_paths prefix would cover them. The narrower rule wins, because the broad one is the one written in a hurry.

allowed_commands.description: argv[0] names. A contract that allows a shell allows everything, so a shell name here is refused by the policy rather than accepted quietly.

network.description: Default denied. `allowlist` is one of the actions that needs an approval token bound to this contract.

network_allowlist.description: Hosts, when network is allowlist. Enforced by the host; the runner records what was declared so a task that reached elsewhere is legible afterwards.

budgets.description: A contract may declare LESS than atlas.yaml/agent_policy/default_budgets and never more; the policy reads the lower of the two.

approval_required.description: Actions this task expects to need approval for. The policy adds every action in agent_policy/approval/required_for whether or not it is listed here, so omitting one does not buy a pass.

base_commit.description: The commit the plan was made against. An approval token is bound to it, so the token dies when the base moves.

status.description: `planned` is what a runner accepts; every other value is written by the runner. `controls_verified` is the honest verdict of a run that exercised every control and did not run the gates — a dry run that said `verified` would be the exact lie this record exists to refuse.

outcome.description: Written by the runner, never by the planner. Its presence in a contract submitted as `planned` is refused.

repo_path.description: Repository-relative, no leading slash, no traversal. A path is refused at the grammar before any policy reads it, because a traversal that reaches the evaluator has already been normalised by somebody.

command_name.description: argv[0] only. Arguments are not part of the allowance; a command is allowed or it is not.

gates.description: One row per planned gate, including the ones that did NOT run. A gate missing from this list and a gate that passed are the same absence otherwise, which is the shape this whole record exists to refuse.

environment.description: The machine the gates ran on. Two agents reporting the same gate as passed under materially different toolchains is the failure; the fingerprint is what makes those two records distinguishable.

sandbox_unobserved.description: The sandbox_requirements rows this runner cannot see. Printed rather than omitted, so a task that ran outside a sandbox never reads as one that ran inside it.
